title: Replace source-pattern settings tests with behavioral multi-window regressions
description:
tests/settingsWindowSync.test.mjs and tests/tabWindowScope.test.mjs primarily assert source-code text patterns. They can pass while runtime event ordering, cached state, or DOM updates remain broken, as seen in recent browser-only regressions.

Add behavior-level tests using a fake chrome.storage.onChanged emitter and realistic DOM/control stubs, or a focused browser harness where needed. Verify: settings changed in one context update controls and appearance in another; all-windows/current-window changes alter the actual chrome.tabs.query arguments and rerender; custom-image upload/delete invalidation updates open windows; and background/theme updates handle asynchronous ordering without stale UI. Keep only minimal source-shape assertions where they protect package parity.

The task is complete when the tests fail against the pre-fix behavior, pass against the corrected implementation, and the complete suite remains green.
label: Maintenance

activity.content:
Replaced the source-pattern settings suites with behavior-level regressions driven by a shared fake chrome.storage.onChanged emitter. The tests now execute the production storage callbacks, appearance loader, render scheduler, and workspace render function against control/container stubs. Coverage verifies cross-window control and appearance sync, real all-windows/current-window chrome.tabs.query arguments plus rerenders, custom-image upload/delete invalidation in open settings and Meridian windows, and latest-wins theme/background async ordering.

Validation:
- Focused corrected-runtime tests: 4/4 pass
- Same tests on pre-fix parent beb506b: 4/4 fail for the expected missing behaviors
- Complete suite: 155/155 pass
- Runtime JavaScript syntax checks: pass
- Manifest parsing: pass
- Packaged runtime parity: pass via the complete suite
- git diff --check: pass
